uutiset.t: Why the AI Panic May Be Premature
uutiset.s: Markets are in a panic over the AI trade. So why is ex-trader and Bloomberg macro strategist Mark Cudmore so bullish on stocks? (Source: Bloomberg)

uutiset.t: Oil Rises as Houthis Attack Two Saudi Ports on Red Sea
uutiset.s: Oil extended gains as Iran-backed Houthi rebels continued to target Saudi Arabia, including a refinery at Ras Tanura and the Red Sea ports of Jeddah and Jazan. Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates said it plans to expand power and water desalination on its eastern coast, beyond the Strait of Hormuz,

uutiset.t: US Tariff Plan Raises Stakes for India to Clinch Trade Deal
uutiset.s: The US plans to impose a 17% tariff on Indian goods, lower than regional peers like Vietnam, Malaysia and Bangladesh. The rate would be hiked to 25% if the country fails to secure a deal, according to a statement from the US Trade Representative. This puts pressure on India to agree to a trade deal

uutiset.t: Tim Hortons China Is Said to Weigh Options Including Stake Sale
uutiset.s: TH International Ltd., which operates Tim Hortons coffee shops in Greater China, is exploring options that may lead to a stake sale, according to people familiar with the matter.

uutiset.t: Chinese Carmakers Double Sales in Europe on Hybrid Demand
uutiset.s: Chinese automakers maintained their rapid advance in Europe last month, with registrations more than doubling ahead of a cap on hybrid vehicle imports from the country.

uutiset.t: Turkey’s Traders See Slower Rate Cut Pace as Reserves Shrink
uutiset.s: Traders are dialing back bets on a December interest-rate cut in Turkey following a sharp drop in central bank reserves, raising concerns that policymakers may have a harder time supporting the lira.

uutiset.t: Stocks and Bonds to Watch as Spain’s Voters Head to the Polls
uutiset.s: Spain’s high-flying stocks have plenty riding on this weekend’s election, with the prospect of a change in government leaving sectors such as banks and utilities with the most at stake.

The Bank of Korea resumed raising interest rates, lifting its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 3.25%. The hike follows a pause in October after back-to-back increases in July and August. Bloomberg's Denny Thomas has the key takeaways from the BOK decision. (Source: Bloomberg)

uutiset.t: Rupee Options Signal Bullish Shift for First Time Since February
uutiset.s: An options-market gauge of the relative cost of hedging against rupee weakness versus strength has turned negative for the first time since February, signaling growing optimism about the Indian currency.

uutiset.t: Xpeng President on Carmaker's Robot Push
uutiset.s: Brian Gu, Vice Chairman & President at Xpeng, discusses humanoid robotics as the carmaker's next growth driver. He speaks exclusively on "Bloomberg: The China Show.” (Source: Bloomberg)

uutiset.t: Canada Pitches Infrastructure Plan to UAE Investors
uutiset.s: Canada is entering a shifting global order from a position of strength, Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne told Bloomberg TV in Dubai. He’s urging Middle Eastern investors to deploy long-term capital into the country’s infrastructure plan. (Source: Bloomberg)

uutiset.t: DHL's Venter: Supply Chain Resilience Is Key to Growth
uutiset.s: DHL Supply Chain CEO Hendrik Venter says resilience is becoming a strategic advantage, as tariffs and geopolitical disruptions make global supply chains more complex. uutiset.t: China-Backed Pakistan Exchange Prepares to Launch Stock Options
uutiset.s: The Pakistani bourse is looking to introduce equity options next year, giving investors another tool to bet on a market that’s tripled over the past three years.

uutiset.t: Adani Firms Plan Public Bond Sale to Raise at Least $220 Million
uutiset.s: Two companies controlled by Indian billionaire Gautam Adani are looking to sell public bonds to raise at least 20 billion rupees ($220 million), according to people familiar with the matter, which would boost the nation’s subdued domestic public debt market.

uutiset.t: Japan Life Insurers Complicate Yen Fight With Record Low Hedging
uutiset.s: Japan’s concerted push to bolster the yen is running into a major headwind, after the nation’s biggest life insurers slashed their currency hedging to a record low in the fiscal first half.
